surfaced_pitfalls.detail: citation_columns (crates/jit/src/domain/artifact_classifier.rs:967) is a plain substring find of the moving artifact's repository-relative source path in each scanned line. Every destination is destination_root + "/" + source, so a citation that correctly names the archived destination still contains the bare source path as a trailing substring and still warns, at a column shifted by exactly the length of the inserted destination-root prefix. Measured on both repointing issues: warning counts unchanged (5 and 3), columns shifted by 35 and 39 characters respectively. The warning is advisory and changes no action, blocker, or eligibility, so nothing is blocked by it.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: OPEN as a product observation, NOT a criterion violation. REQ-08 requires reporting every occurrence of a moving artifact's path in the scan universe, and a corrected citation does contain such an occurrence, so the letter of the criterion is met by reporting it. Candidate follow-up: a warning that distinguishes a bare citation from one already naming the destination. LEAD TRAP: the wave-6 dispatch prompts for cf0f0014 and 80e08e0f told the workers to confirm the warnings disappear after the repoint. That test is unsatisfiable. The correct acceptance test is that the citation names the destination the plan reports.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: the plan-doc location resolver has no production caller, so REQ-03's substitution is latent
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: resolve_plan_doc_location, load_plan_content, and project_plan_doc in crates/jit/src/commands/plan_doc.rs are reached only from that module's own tests. No re-export in commands/mod.rs or lib.rs, no CLI arm, no caller in crates/server/, and project_plan_doc calls project() rather than the reverse. The condition predates d2870182: it holds at base commit f4e142b8 too. What IS live from the module is PLAN_DOC_LABEL, read by planning_node_plan_path (commands/validate.rs:2293) — jit validate locates a plan from the planning node's recorded DocumentReference, not by re-deriving the template's location. PlanDocError's main.rs downcast arm is wired but unreachable because nothing in production constructs it.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: OPEN as a product observation, NOT a criterion violation. d2870182's REQ-03 names the resolver and the resolver now substitutes the field, so the criterion is met; none of the epic's 15 [hard] criteria names plan-doc resolution reachability. Reconcile against the epic criteria before the epic gate; expected to remain a genuine follow-up. If a future issue reintroduces a derive-the-location path, it will resolve {container.dir} to the apply engine's directory and reject an undeclared area without further work.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: pre-existing stale doc comments surface in files an issue rewrites
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: PLAN_DOC_LABEL's doc comment (plan_doc.rs:51-52) claimed the template's plan_doc_location is the creation-time default 'used by jit apply plan when first writing this reference'. Apply attaches no document reference at all — crates/jit/tests/fast_docs_templates/template_apply_tests.rs:243-247 asserts neither node carries a plan-labelled ref. The worker flagged it rather than fixing it, on the correct ground that its own change did not invalidate it.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: CLOSED in d2870182 (commit 33e86a2b) at the lead's direction. The repository rule about sweeping stale text covers text a change invalidates; a pre-existing falsehood in a file the issue otherwise rewrites is cheaper to fix in place than to leave for a reviewer to rediscover. Lead pattern for the remaining waves: when a worker flags pre-existing staleness inside its own footprint, direct the fix rather than deferring it.

lead_notes.subject: b4d1a2c8 cannot run as a standard worktree worker
lead_notes.detail: Renaming dev/archive/a9b5dd08-use-strategic-label-slugs-in-archive-directory-n to dev/archive/a9b5dd08 orphans the one document link on issue a9b5dd08 (`jit doc list a9b5dd08` -> path under the old directory), so REQ-05's whole-repository validation fails unless the link is repointed. That repoint is a .jit/ write, which the standard worker constraint forbids, and .jit/issues/*.json diverging on a branch does not merge. The manifest footprint (creates dev/archive/a9b5dd08, touches the old dir) omits the .jit change.
lead_notes.decision: The lead executes b4d1a2c8 directly on main: git mv, repoint the document link, `jit archive` preview to confirm single-destination convergence (REQ-03), then `jit validate` (REQ-05). Same reasoning that sends wave 8's 24 archive-sweep issues to sequential execution on main.

lead_notes.subject: the epic's own description cites the title-slugged directory as evidence
lead_notes.detail: 8e071e18's Background and Notes name `dev/archive/a9b5dd08-use-strategic-label-slugs-in-archive-directory-n/` as the counter-example proving the naming defect. After b4d1a2c8 renames it, that path no longer exists. dev/active/8e071e18-investigation.md cites it too.
lead_notes.decision: Leave both. The investigation is a dated planning record, and editing the epic's description is an escalation (policy item 3) for a historical evidence citation whose point survives the rename. Raise it only if a reviewer or the holistic-review gate cites it.

lead_notes.subject: verify-commit-builds.sh does not compile test code
lead_notes.detail: 6aa82c0b added citation_scan_roots to DocumentationConfig while 22c11e40 constructed that struct in a test helper in the new domain/artifact_directory.rs. Each branch was green alone; the merge did not compile its test code. scripts/verify-commit-builds.sh still exited 0, because it runs cargo build --workspace, which never compiles #[cfg(test)] items. The break surfaced only as an editor diagnostic and was fixed by the lead in 8afdb018.
lead_notes.decision: After merging a wave, run an actual cargo test compile before gating. The merge-commit verifier is necessary but not sufficient. Worth considering whether the worktree-dispatch protocol's Step 5 should name a test-compiling verifier.

lead_notes.subject: host disk exhaustion from accumulated worktree build artifacts
lead_notes.detail: The host root filesystem reached 100% (0 bytes free) mid-wave. cargo-ci's provenance and budget steps are the only ones needing multi-GB scratch; both failed with EMPTY diagnostic files, which is the signature of failed writes rather than assertions. 39 agent worktrees held ~170G of target/, plus 1365 stale scratch dirs in ~/.cache/jit-cargo-ci-tmp. Lead reclaimed 153G.
lead_notes.decision: RESOLVED this session. Reclaimed 153G of build artifacts, then removed 49 worktrees whose branches are fully merged into main (branches preserved - all 113 worktree-agent-* branches still exist; only checkouts removed). Disk 0 -> 168G free. .agents/worktrees/ now holds only lead-install-clean and steward-v1-readiness (unmerged salvage). The mechanism is unchanged, so prune at the end of every wave: confirm no cargo/rustc processes, check git branch --no-merged main for salvage commits, remove only worktrees whose branch is merged, and clear ~/.cache/jit-cargo-ci-tmp/*. Structural fix filed as be005f64 under milestone v1.1, outside this epic. tmpfs was evaluated and rejected: the workspace exceeds this host's 31G RAM and a prior session already recorded /tmp (16G) being exhausted by large builds.

lead_notes.subject: lead shell cwd drifted into a worker worktree and wrote .jit there
lead_notes.detail: After `cd .agents/worktrees/agent-2ac35e8e && git merge main`, the Bash tool's cwd persisted. Every later command ran in that worktree. `jit issue update f2cac2bd --state done` transitioned the issue inside the WORKTREE's .jit, and the follow-up `jit issue status` read the worktree's .jit — where the wave-5 gate runs do not exist, because .jit/gate-runs records are tracked but the new ones were not yet committed, so a worktree checked out at 36defd8a has none of them. The reported symptom was alarming and completely false: every wave-5 gate appeared to revert from passed/failed to pending and ~2h of gate evidence looked deleted. Nothing was lost; main was intact throughout. The tell was `git reflog` showing the worker branch's history instead of main's, and the worktree carrying the same two modified .jit files main appeared to carry.
lead_notes.decision: Reverted the two stray files in the worktree with `git checkout --` before its rework worker could commit them, and notified that worker. Use `git -C <path>` for worktree git operations rather than `cd`, since it never mutates the shell's cwd. For `jit`, which has no -C equivalent, prefix the command with an explicit `cd /home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time &&` every time. Before trusting any surprising .jit reading, run `pwd` first. This is the session-2 trap recurring in the same session that recorded it.

lead_notes.subject: wave 6 is dispatched in two groups against two different base SHAs

Group A (e2902949, 67345efd, 9ca124f9, ef2bd13c, cf0f0014, 80e08e0f) is anchored at 59b39c26; group B (the six skill conversions) at 192cac9a, after the lead landed d9e70703 on main between the two dispatches. lead_notes.subject: the stale-binary guard is narrower than sessions 1-2 assumed
lead_notes.detail: crates/jit/src/domain/build_provenance.rs refuses a verdict only when binary identity is established AND either the build was dirty or a DECLARED BUILD-INPUT path changed. BINARY_BUILD_INPUTS is Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, crates/jit/Cargo.toml, crates/jit/Cargo.lock, crates/jit/build.rs, crates/jit/src/, profiles/jit-dogfood/, scripts/hooks/pre-commit, scripts/hooks/pre-push. A bare HEAD move past the build commit is NOT staleness.
lead_notes.decision: Reinstall only when a commit since the build touched one of those paths. Wave 7 DID touch crates/jit/src/ (d2870182), so a reinstall is required here. Wave 8's archive executions write only dev/ and .jit/, neither a build input, so the 24 sequential runs should not each need a reinstall — verify empirically at the first sweep rather than assuming, and fall back to reinstalling per commit if a verdict is refused.
